column3: The Hebrew makes the tongue speak at the palate; BSB describes an address on the tip of the tongue.
The Hebrew describes being pinched off from clay; BSB says formed from clay.
The Hebrew names his pressure or weight; BSB names his hand.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here; BSB explicitly names God.
The Hebrew refers to his words without explicitly naming a man asking questions; BSB says He answers nothing a man asks.
The Hebrew numbers the speech once and twice; BSB describes one way and another.
The Hebrew describes sealing discipline; BSB describes terrifying them with warnings.
The Hebrew names a deed without a separate word for wrong and describes covering pride; BSB says wrongdoing and keeping him from pride.
The Hebrew names those bringing death without a separate word for messengers; BSB supplies messengers of death.
The Hebrew names a ransom without an explicit possessive; BSB calls it his ransom.
The Hebrew compares the flesh as fresher than youth; BSB says refreshed like a child’s.
The Hebrew has his soul and his life in the third person; BSB uses my soul and I.
The Hebrew repeats light in describing illumination with life’s light; BSB uses enlightened and light.
